'''Colin Edward Webb''' (born 9 December 1937) is a British physicist and former [[University of Oxford]] professor specialising in [[laser]]s.

==Education==
Webb was educated at the [[University of Nottingham]] (BSc) and [[Oriel College, Oxford]] (DPhil).{{cn|date=October 2024}}

==Career==
After working at [[Bell Labs]] in [[Murray Hill, New Jersey]], Webb returned to Oxford as a [[research fellow]] in physics at the [[Clarendon Laboratory]] in 1968, and was appointed to a university lectureship in 1971, becoming [[Reader (academic rank)|reader]] in 1990 and professor in 1992. He was head of Atomic and Laser Physics from 1995 to 1999 and became an emeritus professor in 2002.  [[Jesus College, Oxford]], appointed him to a [[Oxbridge Fellow|Fellowship]] in 1973; he became a senior research fellow in 1988 and an emeritus fellow in 2005.  Webb has supervised more than 35 DPhil students.<ref name=ox>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jesus.ox.ac.uk/about-jesus-college/our-community/people/professor-colin-webb/|title = Professor Colin Webb}}</ref>  In 1977, he founded Oxford Lasers, a company that began to manufacture high-power copper lasers and today focuses on high-speed imaging and laser micro-machining technology.<ref name=ox />

==Research==
Webb is considered a pioneer in British laser research and has made significant contributions in the areas of hollow cathode metal-vapor lasers,<ref name=Piper1972>{{cite journal|last1=Piper|first1=J.A.|last2=Collins|first2=G.J. |last3=Webb|first3=C.E.| title=CW laser oscillation in singly ionized iodine|journal=Applied Physics Letters|volume=21|issue=5|year=1972|pages=203–205|doi=10.1063/1.1654344|bibcode=1972ApPhL..21..203P}}</ref>
<ref name=GillWebb1977>{{cite journal|last1=Gill|first1=P|last2=Webb|first2=C E|title=Electron energy distributions in the negative glow and their relevance to hollow cathode lasers|journal=Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics|volume=10|issue=3|year=1977|pages=299–301|doi=10.1088/0022-3727/10/3/010|bibcode=1977JPhD...10..299G|s2cid=250755096}}</ref> [[copper vapour laser]]s,<ref name=hpdl /> high-power copper vapour laser-pumped [[dye lasers]],<ref name=hpdl />  and [[excimer lasers]].<ref name="CaroGower1982">{{cite journal|last1=Caro|first1=R G|last2=Gower|first2=M C|last3=Webb|first3=C E|title=A simple tunable KrF laser system with narrow bandwidth and diffraction-limited divergence|journal=Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics|volume=15|issue=5|year=1982|pages=767–773|doi=10.1088/0022-3727/15/5/007|bibcode=1982JPhD...15..767C|s2cid=250810983 }}</ref>  His work on hollow-cathode metal-vapor lasers led to the discovery of numerous new laser transitions in the visible spectrum.<ref name=Piper1972 /><ref name=Piper1973>{{cite journal|last1=Piper|first1=J.A.|last2=Webb|first2=C.E. |title=A hollow cathode device for CW helium-metal vapour laser systems|journal=Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics |volume=6|issue=4|year=1973|pages=400–407|doi=10.1088/0022-3727/6/4/306|bibcode=1973JPhD....6..400P|s2cid=250809897 }}</ref>

His publications include (as editor in chief) ''Handbook of Laser Technology and Applications'' (2003) as well as various papers on lasers and laser mechanisms in academic journals<ref name=Who>{{Who's Who | title=WEBB, Prof Colin Edward| id = U39146 | volume = 2016 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref> and specialised books.<ref name=hpdl>C. E. Webb, "High-power dye lasers pumped by copper vapor lasers", Chapter 5. {{cite web |url=http://www.opticsjournal.com/hpdl.htm |title=High Power Dye Lasers |accessdate=2009-10-07 |publisher=Springer |editor= [[F. J. Duarte]] |location=Berlin |year=1991|url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090507093232/http://www.opticsjournal.com/hpdl.htm |archivedate=2009-05-07 }}</ref> He has also co-authored a textbook on laser physics in 2010, with Simon Hooker of Oxford.<ref>S. Hooker and C. E. Webb, ''Laser Physics'', (Oxford University Press, 2010) [http://www.physics.ox.ac.uk/Users/hooker/LaserPhysics/reviews.html]</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Webb was appointed a [[Member of the Order of the British Empire]] in 2000.  He was awarded the [[Duddell Medal and Prize]] (now called the Gabor Medal and Prize) in 1985 by the [[Institute of Physics]] and delivered the [[Paterson Lecture]] of the [[Royal Society]] in 1999.<ref name=Who/> He won the [[Richard Glazebrook Medal and Prize]] in 2001.

He is a [[OSA Fellow|Fellow of the Optical Society of America]] {{fact|date=May 2016}} and was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1991|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1991]].<ref name=frs>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117012412/https://royalsociety.org/people/colin-webb-12501/|archivedate=2015-11-17|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/colin-webb-12501/|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|title=Professor Colin Webb MBE FRS}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{quote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925220834/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |date=September 25, 2015 |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies }}}}</ref> He is also a [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]].
